items.title: Alice Zeno Interview, 1958-12-10
items.q: And an old man they called Pajaco. And he was a Senegalian. And he translated, you know. And that's where my great-grandmother then began to learn how to speak.

ctx.x: Because her mother came there and was told from her country, you see. When she says... She said he was eight years old. But she couldn't speak nothing. But they had an old man at Charles Perrette. That bought all the Senegalian niggers that he could. And an old man they called Pajaco. And he was a Senegalian. And he translated, you know. And that's where my great-grandmother then began to learn how to speak. But she said she was eight years old. And they had gone to bed by the... By the... Not lagume. Lagume is…
My great-grandmother. And she remembered them. When the slave traders came there.
